title: Is Your Phone Line Ready for Khareef's Final Surge?
seoTitle: Is Your Phone Line Ready for Khareef's Final Surge?
excerpt: Khareef's Gulf wave is filling Salalah's hotels, clinics and showrooms with calls at every hour. Here's the two-week, dated plan to make sure yours doesn't buckle before Mawlid.
seoDescription: Khareef has brought GCC visitors flooding into Salalah. Here's a two-week, dated plan to get your business phone line ready before the peak hits.

blocks.text: Khareef has already brought 472,449 visitors to Dhofar since the season began on 21 June, and 78,356 of them travelled in from the rest of the Gulf. Most of the calls asking about rooms, appointments and rentals now land on your phone after dark. You have about two weeks before the Mawlid holiday adds another travel bump, which is exactly enough time to check whether your phone line can carry what khareef is about to throw at it.
Why the lines are busier than usual

segments.text: Khareef season runs from around 21 June to 21 September, and this year's numbers show the pull is real. Dhofar's tourism figures for the first six weeks put visitor numbers at 472,449, a rise of 6.9% on last year, with air arrivals up 9.6%. Visitors from the rest of the Gulf, mostly Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Kuwait, made up 78,356 of that total, 16.6% of all visitors and a clear rise on last year's 69,801.

Every one of those visitors calls somewhere before they arrive: a hotel to hold a room, a clinic to book a check up for a parent travelling with them, a rental company to confirm a car, a tour desk to ask what is still running this week. If your business sits anywhere near that chain, your phone has already picked up the extra load, whether your roster has caught up or not.

blocks.text: Who is actually calling your desk

segments.text: The caller on the other end of khareef season is rarely the customer your team handles every other month of the year. Expect calls from:

items.text: Gulf families booking multiple rooms or villas for a week, often calling late at night after their own workday ends
Families travelling down from Muscat and other parts of the country confirming weekend plans around the greenery
Tour operators and drivers checking last minute availability for groups
Grown children living in the Gulf booking a clinic appointment for a parent visiting Salalah
Dealership and rental customers wanting a car serviced or handed over before or after a khareef trip

segments.text: Many of these calls arrive in Gulf Arabic dialects that sit a little differently from the Omani Arabic your team hears every day, mixed with English and sometimes a driver's Hindi or Urdu. None of that is new for Salalah. What is new this stretch is how many of these calls land after your day shift has already gone home.

blocks.text: The calls that decide whether your rooms, clinics and service bays fill this khareef mostly arrive after your day team has clocked out.

segments.text: Most Salalah front desks run lean overnight: one person handling check ins, the safe and the phone all at once. When a Gulf family calls at eleven to ask about a room for four nights, that call competes with a guest standing at the counter. Something has to wait, and it is usually the phone.

Missed calls at this hour rarely turn into a voicemail worth calling back. A caller who cannot get through tends to try the next hotel, clinic or rental desk on their list instead of waiting. What finally closes that gap for a lot of Salalah teams has less to do with hiring more night staff and more to do with matching the desk's tools to when the calls actually happen, which the plan below walks through.

blocks.text: The two week plan before Mawlid

segments.text: You have from now, 15 August, to the Mawlid holiday, expected around Thursday, 27 August 2026 and subject to the official moon sighting announcement, to get ready. Use the two weeks like this:

items.text: 15 to 17 August: pull the last two weeks of call logs and mark how many calls arrived after 8pm. This one number tells you whether the problem below is worth solving.
18 to 20 August: brief the front desk, call and booking teams on the extra evening volume, and agree who covers the phone between 8pm and 1am.
21 to 23 August: confirm the Mawlid holiday roster now, since travel enquiries do not pause for a public holiday even when your team is off.
24 to 26 August: test whatever after hours setup you choose, a rota, a shared inbox or an automated line, against a few real evening calls.
27 to 29 August: review what came in over the holiday weekend and decide if evening coverage should run through to when khareef ends around 21 September.

segments.text: Start with the call log, not with new hires. Most Salalah teams do not need a bigger night shift for the whole year; they need their existing hours to stretch further for the two or three peak weeks that are left in khareef.

If your after hours calls are a handful, a shared inbox and a clear rota might be enough. If they look like what Rashid found, twenty or more a night in three languages, a rota alone will not hold. This is where some front desks are testing an Omani Arabic customer care line such as

, which answers in the dialect a Gulf caller actually speaks, holds the line after the desk closes, and leaves the morning team a written note of every call instead of a guess. Whatever you choose, check the pattern first: a peak hours view like a

blocks.title: Your two-minute check
paragraphs: Pull your call log for the last three nights and count how many calls landed after 9pm.
Ask the night shift how many callers they had to put on hold, or lost, while checking in a guest at the same time.
Note whether last week's after hours calls came in Arabic dialects your team found tricky, or in English, Hindi or Urdu.
If the after hours count is climbing, decide this week whether it needs a rota change or an automated line, not after Mawlid has passed.

items.q: Is 27 August definitely the Mawlid holiday this year?
items.a: The government has listed Thursday, 27 August 2026 on the 2026 holiday calendar, but Oman confirms the exact Islamic date closer to the day once the moon sighting is announced.

items.q: Does khareef only matter for hotels?
items.a: No. Clinics, dealerships, rental firms and tour desks across Dhofar see the same after hours jump while visitors are in town.

items.q: How long should extra evening coverage run?
items.a: Khareef typically runs to around 21 September, so plan coverage through to then rather than stopping the day after Mawlid.

segments.text: Khareef is not a surprise, and neither is the call volume it brings every year. The businesses that come out of this season with full rooms, booked slots and satisfied customers are the ones that checked their phone against the wave before it hit, not after it passed. Two weeks is enough time to know exactly where you stand and fix what needs fixing.
